payload.root_cause: Off-by-one loop bound in `Cart.subtotal()` (pyshop/cart.py:52-56): it iterates `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)` instead of `range(len(self.items))`, so the last line item in the cart is never added to the total. With the reported cart (2 mugs = 25.00, 1 lamp = 39.99, 3 pens = 3.00) only the first two lines are summed: 25.00 + 39.99 = 64.99, dropping the pens line and producing $64.99 instead of $67.99. The bug propagates to `order_total()`, which calls `cart.subtotal()` (pyshop/cart.py:69). Cart.add() and LineItem.total are correct — the defect is purely the loop bound.
evidence: pyshop/cart.py:52-56 — `def subtotal(self): total = Decimal("0"); for i in range(len(self.items) - 1): total += self.items[i].total; return to_money(total)` — the range excludes the final index, skipping the last LineItem.
pyshop/cart.py:34-43 — `Cart.add` correctly appends one LineItem per distinct SKU, so a 3-product cart has len(self.items) == 3 and items[2] (the pens) is skipped by the loop.
Arithmetic check: 2×12.50 + 1×39.99 = 64.99 (observed wrong value); adding the skipped 3×1.00 = 3.00 gives 67.99 (expected value), confirming the missing last line.
tests/test_cart.py:21-25 — `test_subtotal_sums_all_lines` adds the same three lines and asserts Decimal("67.99"), matching the report.
pyshop/cart.py:69 — `subtotal = cart.subtotal()` inside `order_total`, so shipping/tax/total are also computed from the under-counted subtotal.
